answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral in an escrow, so creating aliases does not create free voting power. When k identities coordinate equivocation, correlated evidence raises their aggregate penalty as O(k^2); upon detection, controlling the swarm incurs an exponential capital-loss multiplier, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery through rebonding. The copper thread of shared control becomes evidence, and every summit of coordinated voting increases exposure rather than influence.
